newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips slightly, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips slightly, seen consolidating.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ambled to end Thursday midsession slightly lower on light trade selling.
Traders said midday volume was an unimpressive at 2,349 lots with players adopting a wait-and-see attitude in the absence of fresh fundamental inputs.
One view was that the market was likely to consolidate at current levels before retreating if funds liquidate their large long positions.
"It is holding around these levels, reflecting over what happened in the past few days," said one trader.
Benchmark September wandered in a tight four stg range before ending the morning business at the top of the range at 1,115 stg per tonne, a three stg loss.
But July recovered by the closing bell to end midday just two stg up at 1,100 after a low of 1,094.
Analysts said September would really need to drop below Tuesday's low 1,097 to spark any real concern, and below 1,065 to negate the bullish move.
Fundamentally, traders are awaiting early forecasts of the 1997/98 Ivorian crop but with the current "silly season" in cocoa, they said they could expect a lot of crop rumours.

Early 1997/98 crop estimates vary from a 785,000 tonnes-mark (main crop) by U.S.-based crop analyst Hans Kilian, according to traders, to a more optimistic 1.1 million tonnes for the whole of 1997/98 by Swiss chocolate giant Callebaut Barry, which has two factories in Ivory Coast.
Ivory Coast, the world's largest producer, notched up a record 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
A dry season in July and August which is a strong determinant of the survival rate of pods now setting on trees could be longer than usual if an El Nino weather patterns emerged by then, one said.
